slides.title: Preserving Metadata with functools.wraps
slides.prompt: Applying a decorator without wrapping metadata causes the decorated function to lose its original name (`__name__`) and docstring (`__doc__`). `@functools.wraps` copies these attributes from the original function onto the wrapper.

slides.title: Importing wraps Decorator
slides.prompt: Fill in the module name used to import the 'wraps' decorator utility.

slides.title: Consequence of Omitting wraps
slides.prompt: What happens to `func.__name__` if `@wraps(func)` is NOT used inside a decorator?
options: The function name defaults to 'wrapper' (or the name of the inner closure function)
Python raises an AttributeError at runtime
The decorated function cannot be called
slides.correctAnswer: The function name defaults to 'wrapper' (or the name of the inner closure function)

slides.title: Decorating Wrapper Function
slides.prompt: Fill in the target argument passed to `@wraps()` decorator inside the wrapper definition.

slides.title: Accessing Original Unwrapped Function
slides.prompt: How can you access the original undecorated function when `@wraps` was used?
options: Via the `__wrapped__` attribute on the decorated function
It is impossible to retrieve the original function
slides.correctAnswer: Via the `__wrapped__` attribute on the decorated function
